  "rationale": "The book applies its cross-text method rigorously: it first separates lamp oil from anointing oil via the inventory in Exodus 25:6 and the distinct preparations/uses in Exodus 27:20 vs. 30:22-33, then shows that Spirit-anointing texts therefore cannot supply the definition for the virgins' vessels. Proverbs 21:20 already pairs oil (stored by the wise, spent by the fool) with the same wise/fool contrast Matthew uses. The buy-and-keep language of Matthew 25:9 is fixed by Proverbs 23:23 to truth/wisdom/instruction, which Scripture itself equates with the law kept and done (Psalm 119:142; Psalm 111:10; Deuteronomy 4:6; Job 28:28). Psalms 141:5 and 27:5-9 further identify oil with received correction and hearty counsel that is worked inward. The result is Spirit-produced fruit (Ezekiel 36:27; Galatians 5:22; Philippians 2:13) stored as proven obedience—the fuel that turns the lamp (commandment, Proverbs 6:23) into visible light (Matthew 5:16). The common Holy-Spirit reading is not merely alternative but contradicted by the parable's own mechanics (non-transferable, finite, buyable only in advance), which fit stored obedience and do not fit the freely given, non-measurable Spirit. No counter-text breaks the pattern, and Zechariah 4 supplies the Spirit as power behind the work without equating the flowing oil itself with the Spirit. The identification is therefore better supported by the gathered scriptural relationships than the popular pneumatological default.",
